name: Web Recon
summary: Fingerprints web pages: favicon hashes in the forms Shodan, Censys and other search services index, HHHash of the response header names, and a hash of the HTML tag structure. Desktop only.
description:
Fingerprints to pivot on when operators rotate domains, IP addresses and certificates but reuse what sits underneath: a phishing kit's favicon, a server stack's header layout, a storefront template's markup. A fingerprint shared by otherwise unrelated hosts is a lead for clustering them (Tor and clear web, staging and production, a clone and its original).

**Who sees it:** the target. Every plugin requests the selected site directly from the analyst's machine, one request per URL, with no cookies or credentials. No third-party service is queried; the hashes are looked up on the search services separately.

**Read results with care:**
- A common default icon (a framework's, a hosting panel's) matches unrelated sites. An HHHash reflects the server stack, so a shared one points at the same deployment practice.
- `phash` and `dhash` are compared by bit distance, not equality; Krawetz counts 10 or fewer differing bits as a likely variant. Censys and VirusTotal do not document their perceptual hashes, so equivalence with their values is not established.
- HHHash fingerprints any status, 403 and 404 included: an error page still shows the stack. The DOM hash ignores text and attributes, so a template keeps its hash when its text, branding or language change.

**Data and licences:** none shipped; every value is computed from the site's own response. HHHash is computed as the reference `hhhash` package does (https://github.com/adulau/HHHash), so values compare with other tools'. The DOM hash is the dom-hash technique from The Art of Pivoting.

**Source:** https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-web-recon (Apache-2.0)

plugins.name: Favicon Hash
plugins.description: Fetches /favicon.ico from the host of each selected URL and creates a web.favicon_hash node linked by "has favicon". A favicon hash identifies the icon file a site serves, and each form a search service indexes is its own property. hash_value is the Shodan-style MurmurHash3 searched by Shodan http.favicon.hash, FOFA icon_hash, Censys favicons.hash_shodan and ZoomEye iconhash. mmh3_hex is that value in hex, searched by Criminal IP favicon:. md5 is searched by Censys favicons.hash_md5, ZoomEye iconhash, 360 Quake favicon, Hunter.how favicon_hash, ONYPHE app.favicon.imagemd5 and VirusTotal main_icon_md5. sha256 is searched by Censys favicons.hash_sha256, Netlas http.favicon.hash_sha256 and urlscan.io hash. phash and dhash are perceptual hashes of ICO, PNG and BMP icons, compared by how many of their 64 bits differ. phash is the ImageHash pHash. dhash follows VirusTotal main_icon_dhash, which VirusTotal searches by similarity. Does not follow redirects or read the page for a <link rel="icon">. Desktop only.

web_probe.purpose: Fetch the favicon of each selected site.

plugins.name: HTTP Header Hash (HHHash)
plugins.description: Requests each selected URL over HTTP/1.1 and creates a web.hhhash node with its HHHash (hhh:1: plus the SHA-256 of the response header names in order), linked by "has header hash"; also records the header count and Server value. Does not follow redirects. Desktop only.

web_probe.purpose: Fetch the response headers of each selected site.

plugins.name: DOM Structure Hash
plugins.description: Fetches the HTML of each selected URL and creates a web.dom_hash node with a hash of its HTML tag sequence, linked by "has dom hash". Does not follow redirects. Desktop only.

web_probe.purpose: Fetch the HTML of each selected site.
